title: Khronos DirectionalLight -- KHR_lights_punctual and the metal-rough BRDF, judged on Khronos's published appearance and on the hue the asset states for itself

criterion.says: The purpose of this test model is to verify that the BRDF and microfacet model used by a renderer preserves energy. ... In order to preserve energy it is important that this factor does not add light energy. ... As the lightsource has an intensity of 1 (lumen / m2) and display output can be considered to be candela / m2 it should never be the case that light contribution go above: (Color * Intensity) = [0.9, 0.8, 0.1] - in linear space. ... Lightsource color = RGB[0.9, 0.8, 0.1], Hue of the lightsource = [0.9 / 1.8, 0.8 / 1.8, 0.1 / 1.8] = [0.5, 0.444, 0.0555]. The displayed (concentrated) specuar highlight shall retain this hue.
criterion.note: The asset states in the same paragraph that this is not an exact comparison -- 'this will of course not be an exact measure since values are read and written with different precision' -- so the criterion was never an agreement with any reference. What stays numeric is the hue, computed from our render alone, and the energy half, which moved to a white-furnace integral over our own BRDF in test/unit/render/stages/TheMicrofacetLobeAddsNoEnergy.cpp -- no asset, no oracle, no punctual light. The per-pixel ceiling that used to stand here was a misreading of WHICH QUANTITY the asset bounds: glTF's own Appendix B returns f_spec * N.L = 4.857 at the roughness-0.16 sphere's centre, so a ceiling of 0.9 on outgoing radiance is a test the specification's reference implementation fails, and what an added NDF factor actually breaks is the directional albedo (board:0085). THE ORACLE IS A REFERENCE AGAIN AND WAS NOT BEFORE: the role was cannot-express-the-criterion because Cycles performs no back-face culling for camera rays and this asset is inside-out, so the two sides drew DIFFERENT SURFACES BEHIND ONE SILHOUETTE -- 130746 of 921600 pixels differing at a widest channel delta of 91 codes. The subject is now corrected in the preparer (subjects[0].patch) rather than either renderer, both sides render the corrected bytes, and the disagreement is gone: 0 px disagreeing on coverage, hue error 4.52e-08 over 9217 judged samples.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (`board/`). Khronos's DirectionalLight is a curved, multi-part asset whose silhouette resolves into hundreds of distinct lines, so the construction cannot be written for it. Its acceptance is its own stated invariant and the placement is bounded by the oracle's filter half-width.

subjects.name: DirectionalLight
subjects.notes: Three spheres of one base colour 0.6 at metallic 0 and roughness 0, 0.16 and 0.33, each scaled 3x and placed 0.6 m apart, plus the file's own perspective camera at (0, 0, 2) and one node carrying the KHR_lights_punctual directional light. The light's beam is the node's -Z and the node's rotation is the identity, so it shines straight down the view axis and every sphere is lit head-on -- which puts N, V and L together at the centre of each sphere and makes the specular peak the brightest sample in the frame by construction.

source.pinReason: the same pin every other Khronos subject in this tree carries

patch.why: The asset is inside-out and reproduces its own published appearance only on a renderer that performs no back-face culling. Every one of its 31800 triangles is wound clockwise as seen from outside and every one of its 16122 vertex normals points inward, and no material declares doubleSided -- so glTF requires the near hemisphere of each sphere to be culled, a conforming renderer shades the far one, and the far one's inward normals happen to point back at the camera. Two inversions that cancel are still two errors, and they cancel only for the picture: they do NOT cancel for a visibility ray, which correctly reports that a surface inside a sphere cannot see the light and returns three black discs. Correcting the RENDERER was refused -- un-culling this file would assert a picture the format forbids for it, and would make a winding defect in a generated part unspellable later. Correcting the ASSET produces a file a conforming renderer draws correctly, and both sides of the comparison then render the same corrected bytes.
patch.shouldHaveBeenUpstream: Every triangle wound counter-clockwise as seen from outside and every vertex normal pointing away from its sphere's centre. Either correction alone would have made the defect visible in Khronos's own screenshot; together they hid it. Reportable upstream with both counts, which are recomputed by this preparer on every run and stand in observedBefore below.

triangles.note: 10600 per sphere over three spheres, which share one index accessor

trianglesCounterClockwiseFromOutside.note: cross(v1-v0, v2-v0) against the triangle centroid minus the mesh's vertex mean, over every drawn primitive. Not one triangle of the asset faces outward.

trianglesOfZeroArea.note: Two per sphere, at the pole seam, with a cross product of exactly zero. They have no facing, so no winding makes them point anywhere and the verification excludes them by name rather than admitting a tolerance. A second, separate upstream defect, and they draw nothing.

transforms.note: Swaps the second and third corner of every triangle, in the one shared index accessor, and moves no vertex.

vertexNormals.note: 5374 per sphere over three spheres, each with its own NORMAL accessor

vertexNormalsOutward.note: dot(N, P - the mesh's vertex mean) > 0, over every vertex. It is 0 and not 302: the dot product runs from -0.0734 to -0.0705 with no zero crossing, so the file is consistently inside-out rather than mostly so.

transforms.note: Negates each sphere's own NORMAL accessor. It is a SECOND correction and not part of the first: winding and normals are two independent defects that happened to occur together here, and an asset with only one of them is a case this list still describes.

patch.reportedUpstream: Not yet filed. Owed to KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets against commit 2bac6f8c57bf471df0d2a1e8a8ec023c7801dddf, Models/DirectionalLight, with the four counts in observedBefore: 0 of 31800 triangles counter-clockwise from outside, 0 of 16122 vertex normals outward, 6 triangles of exactly zero area, and 0 of 3 materials declaring doubleSided. The asset reproduces its own published screenshot only on a renderer that performs no back-face culling.
patch.retirementCondition: The preparer already evaluates it every run: observedBefore is RECOMPUTED from the bytes on disk and refused on mismatch, so an upstream asset with consistent outward winding makes this patch red rather than silently redundant. The fetch's sha256 pin is the second, coarser evaluation of the same condition -- any change to upstream's bytes refuses before the patch is reached. The fork cannot be carried forward by nobody's decision.
patch.stillTests: The asset's own criterion is the same sentence after the patch: 'the color of the specular highlight shall retain the same hue as the lightsource'. The correction moves no vertex, changes no material, no roughness and no light, so the BRDF sweep across roughness 0, 0.16 and 0.33 that the asset exists for is untouched -- what changes is which of the two shells behind one silhouette a conforming renderer shades. The declared cost is that this case no longer tests Khronos's exact bytes: it tests our reader and renderer against a corrected subject, which is a smaller claim than the unpatched case made and larger than the three black discs it produced.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render.

camera.note: The file carries exactly one camera and it is the one the asset was authored to be seen through: yfov 0.65, znear 0.3, zfar 5, at (0, 0, 2) with no rotation. Declaring another here would be choosing where the highlight lands, which is the quantity under test.

light.note: THE ONE ASSET CLASS WHERE THE LIGHT CROSSES THE BOUNDARY (board:0085): the criterion is stated in terms of the light in the file -- 'the directional lightsource is defined as: Intensity = 1.0 lumen / m2, Color = [0.9, 0.8, 0.1]' -- so re-declaring it beside the asset would measure our transcription. RAW because glTF's directional intensity in lux IS Blender's Sun Strength in W/m2 perpendicular, one to one, with no conversion in either direction. The importer's sun is then forced to angle 0, which makes it a delta source with no solid angle to sample.

world.note: BLACK, AND THAT IS THE REDUCTION RATHER THAN A LOOK. The factory world is an area source: Cycles samples it, and at one sample per pixel that is a Bernoulli draw on the visible sky fraction rather than a value. With the world at zero the only source left is a delta light, the estimator has no variance, and the two seeds must agree bit for bit. Khronos's criterion is a relation between channels of one render and is invariant to the ambient term, so nothing under test is removed with it.

material.note: The file's own three materials, whole: base colour 0.6, metallic 0, roughness 0 / 0.16 / 0.33. They ARE the subject -- the asset exists to sweep the normal distribution function across those three roughnesses -- so replacing the closure with a Diffuse BSDF, as every other file-coloured case in this tree does, would delete the thing being measured.

default.note: NO TRANSPARENT BOUNCES, and this recipe therefore renders the OUTER surface of a subject a conforming rasteriser culls -- the one place this oracle and this engine are known to disagree, measured and named in test/corpus/prep/in_blender_render.py. Zero bounces still carries direct light: measured on this host, a plane of base colour 0.6 at roughness 0.5 under a sun of strength 1 comes back at 0.23515162 where the glTF BRDF's closed form is 0.23428 -- 0.37 % apart, which is the Principled BSDF's multiscatter GGX against the format's single-scatter one. What zero bounces removes is the indirect term, and what the black world removes is the area source.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed. A delta light with no radius and a world of strength zero leave Cycles no integral to estimate, so the two dumps must agree bit for bit and any difference NAMES the source that still has an area.

statedInvariants.name: highlight_hue
statedInvariants.says: This means that the color of the specular highlight shall retain the same hue as the lightsource. Where hue is the color without reference to how dull or satururated the color is. This value can be calculated by dividing each RGB component by the total.

hue.derivation: each channel of the light's colour over the sum of the three: 0.9/1.8, 0.8/1.8, 0.1/1.8, which is the arithmetic the asset writes out itself

brightestFraction.note: The brightest hundredth of the covered pixels, which is where the concentrated highlights are: the asset says to check THE HIGHLIGHT with a colour picker, so judging every covered pixel would be judging a claim the asset does not make. One per cent of this subject's coverage is several thousand samples, so the count is a distribution and not an anecdote.

maxHueError.note: Sixteen f32 steps at a ratio near 0.5, which is what a chain of about twenty multiplications and one division can round away. There is nothing physical between our value and the light's hue: base colour and F0 are both achromatic here, so every channel is the same BRDF times the light's own colour, and the ratio is the light's hue exactly in real arithmetic.

notes: This is the first case in the tree whose subject is lit at all. It needs KHR_lights_punctual through the reader, a light list rather than one sun, NORMAL through to the draw, and glTF's own metal-rough BRDF evaluated against a direction -- which is the whole of what a punctual light unblocks (board:0123).

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's 31800 indices, i.e. 10600 triangles per sphere over three spheres, of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the file's own camera, recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.

depthProbes.name: middle_sphere_centre

rangeM.derivation: the file's own camera sits at (0, 0, 2) looking down -Z, the middle sphere is at the origin, and its POSITION accessor declares max z = 0.07233947515487671 under a node scale of 3 -- so the nearest point of that sphere on the optical axis is 3 * 0.07233947515487671 = 0.21701842546463013 m from the origin and 2 - 0.21701842546463013 = 1.7829815745353699 m from the eye. The runner recomputes the range from the depth attachment as kNearM / depth times the secant of the angle off boresight, which at the frame centre is 1.0000004 (yfov 0.65, 1280x720).

toleranceM.note: Above the tessellation sagitta and far below the defect it exists to catch. MEASURED, by casting the centre pixel's ray against this mesh's own triangles: the near shell is hit at 1.783038503521493 m, which is 5.693e-05 m outside the analytic sphere -- the chord depth of a facet at this triangle count. The FAR shell is hit at 2.2169608972301384 m, so drawing the wrong surface moves the range by 0.4339 m, 4340 times this tolerance. That is the transformation silhouette, coverage and hue are all invariant under.

depthProbes.says: The picture is of the sphere's NEAR surface. This asset shipped inside-out -- wound clockwise from outside with inward normals -- and a conforming renderer therefore drew the far shell at 2.217 m while the silhouette, the coverage and the hue all agreed with the oracle. Depth is the one criterion that is not invariant under that swap, and it is what checks that the declared patch took.

reductions.because: CYCLES COUPLES ITS DIFFUSE TO THE VIEW AND glTF SPECIFIES THE HALF-VECTOR, and `board:1363` measured the whole of it on a generated sphere with nothing else in the path: our diffuse is Appendix B's `(1 - F(v.h)) * baseColor / pi` term for term, Blender's Principled attenuates by `1 - E(n.v)` -- the specular layer's own directional albedo -- and the two ends of that curve name the mechanism, 0.964 at normal incidence which is `1 - 0.04`, and 0.755 at grazing. **No Blender node graph can reach the microfacet half-vector**: `Fresnel` and `Layer Weight` are functions of `n.v`, so this oracle cannot evaluate the specification this corpus is a corpus for. Bending our lobe towards Blender's would put this tree outside the extension it implements to make a number smaller. THE TWO RENDERS WERE LOOKED AT AND ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE BY EYE -- three olive spheres, same places, same terminators, same highlights -- at p99 5 codes against a bound of 1.
